Regarding the text provided: "The committee has finished its work, and they have submitted its report to the board."

There is a pronoun-antecedent agreement error in the second clause. The antecedent "committee" is a collective noun. In the first clause, it is treated as singular ("its work"). In the second clause, the pronoun "they" treats it as plural, while "its" treats it as singular. To maintain consistency, the pronouns should agree with the antecedent. If the committee is viewed as a single unit (singular), the sentence should be: "The committee has finished its work, and it has submitted its report to the board." If the committee is viewed as individual members (plural), the first clause should be adjusted: "The committee have finished their work, and they have submitted their report to the board." The most standard formal correction, treating the committee as a singular entity, is:

The committee has finished its work, and it has submitted its report to the board.
